questions.q: An occupation in which people render personalised services of a specialised nature, based on professional knowledge and training, is called a ______.
questions.e: Doctors, lawyers and chartered accountants follow a profession, which needs specialised knowledge and membership of a professional body.

questions.q: Industries engaged in the extraction and production of natural resources and the reproduction of living organisms are called ______ industries.
questions.e: Primary industries include extractive industries (mining, fishing) and genetic industries (poultry, nurseries).

questions.q: Which objective of business means producing more output with the given resources, and is essential for its survival and growth?
questions.e: Productivity is the ratio of output to input; every business must aim to keep improving it to stay competitive.

questions.q: A rice trader in Karnal stores paddy after harvest and sells it gradually throughout the year. Warehousing here removes the hindrance of ______.
questions.e: Warehousing preserves goods from the time they are produced until they are needed, removing the hindrance of time; transport removes the hindrance of place.

questions.q: Classify the following industries as per the NCERT classification of industries.
p: (a) Coal mining in Jharkhand is which type of primary industry?
extractive|extractive industry
(b) A sugar mill that refines sugarcane belongs to which type of manufacturing industry?
processing|processing industry
(c) A cement factory that combines limestone, clay and gypsum belongs to which type of manufacturing industry?
synthetical|synthetic|synthetical industry
questions.e: Extractive industries take products from natural sources; processing industries put raw material through successive stages (sugar, paper); synthetical industries combine ingredients into a new product (cement, soap).

questions.q: In a Joint Hindu Family business, the eldest member who controls and manages the business is called the ______.
questions.e: The karta manages the family business and has unlimited liability, while the other coparceners have liability limited to their share.

questions.q: The maximum number of members permitted in a private company is ______.
questions.e: Under the Companies Act, 2013, a private company can have at most 200 members (excluding present and past employees).

questions.q: A partner who contributes capital and shares profits but does not take part in the day-to-day running of the firm is a ______ partner.
questions.e: A sleeping or dormant partner is not known to outsiders as active, but still has unlimited liability.

questions.q: Ravi, a famous cricketer, allows a sports-goods firm to use his name as a partner. He invests no capital, takes no share in profits, but is liable to third parties. Ravi is a ______ partner.
questions.e: A nominal partner only lends his name to the firm; he does not contribute capital or share profits, but remains liable to outsiders.

questions.q: A cooperative society formed to provide loans to its members at low rates of interest is a ______ cooperative society.
questions.e: Credit cooperative societies accept deposits and give loans to members at easy terms, protecting them from moneylenders.

questions.q: Meena runs a small boutique in Jaipur all by herself. She takes all decisions alone and keeps the entire profit. If the business fails, creditors can recover their dues from her personal property.
p: (a) Name the form of business organisation.
sole proprietorship|sole proprietor|sole trader|sole proprietary concern|sole proprietary
(b) What is the nature of Meena's liability?
unlimited|unlimited liability
(c) Is the business a separate legal entity from Meena? (yes/no)
no
questions.e: A sole proprietorship is owned and controlled by one person; the owner and business are the same in law, so the owner's liability is unlimited.

questions.q: A government company is one in which not less than ______ percent of the paid-up share capital is held by the government.
questions.e: A government company has at least 51% of its paid-up capital held by the Central and/or State Government(s).

questions.q: Indian Railways and Posts and Telegraphs are examples of ______ undertakings.
questions.e: Departmental undertakings are run as departments of a ministry and are financed by annual budget appropriations.

questions.q: A public enterprise created by a special Act of Parliament or a State Legislature, which defines its powers and functions, is called a ______.
questions.e: Statutory corporations like LIC are set up under a special Act and enjoy the power of government along with the flexibility of private enterprise.

questions.q: Huge business enterprises that have operations in several countries but are controlled from a headquarters in one country are called global enterprises or ______.
questions.a: multinational corporations|multinational corporation|mncs|mnc|multinational companies|multinational company|transnational corporations
questions.e: Global enterprises or MNCs have huge capital, advanced technology and a worldwide network of operations.

questions.q: An Indian auto-parts firm and a Japanese company pool their resources to form a new company in India, sharing ownership, control, profits and risks. This arrangement is a ______.
questions.e: A joint venture is formed when two or more businesses agree to pool resources for a common purpose and share ownership and control.

questions.q: The insurance principle that requires both parties to disclose all material facts honestly is the principle of utmost good ______.
questions.e: Uberrimae fidei (utmost good faith) means the insured must disclose all material facts, otherwise the contract can be avoided.

questions.q: Under the principle of ______, the insured is only compensated for the actual loss suffered and cannot make a profit from insurance.
questions.e: Indemnity applies to fire and marine insurance: the insurer puts the insured back in the position he was in before the loss, not better.

questions.q: Arjun's insured car is damaged by a truck driven carelessly. After the insurance company compensates Arjun, it gets his right to recover damages from the truck owner. Which principle of insurance applies?
questions.e: Under subrogation, after paying the claim the insurer steps into the shoes of the insured and acquires his rights against third parties.

questions.q: The electronic fund transfer system used for transferring large amounts instantly, on a transaction-by-transaction basis, is called ______.
questions.e: RTGS (Real Time Gross Settlement) settles each transaction individually and instantly, and is meant for high-value transfers.

questions.q: Raghav, a basmati rice exporter in Punjab, stores his stock in a warehouse of the Central Warehousing Corporation and insures the stock against fire.
p: (a) A warehouse owned and managed by the Central Warehousing Corporation is which type of warehouse?
government warehouse|government|government warehouses
(b) Which type of insurance has Raghav taken?
fire insurance|fire
(c) To claim, the fire must be the nearest cause of the loss. Name this principle.
causa proxima|proximate cause|principle of causa proxima
questions.e: Government warehouses are owned by central or state governments (e.g., CWC); under causa proxima the insurer pays only if the proximate cause of loss is the insured peril.

questions.q: In online shopping, the payment method in which the buyer pays in cash when the goods are delivered at the doorstep is called ______.
questions.e: Cash on delivery lets buyers who are wary of online payment pay only after receiving the goods.

questions.q: The term for conducting industry, trade and commerce using computer networks, which is wider than e-commerce, is ______.
questions.e: E-business covers all business functions done online (production, finance, HR), while e-commerce covers only buying and selling.

questions.q: Contracting out a firm's non-core activities, such as payroll or customer support, to outside specialist agencies is called ______.
questions.e: Outsourcing lets a firm focus on its core competencies while specialists handle non-core processes.

questions.q: Neha, a college student in Pune, sells her old bicycle to another student through an online classifieds website. This is an example of ______ commerce.
questions.a: c2c|c to c|customer to customer|consumer to consumer|customer-to-customer
questions.e: When one consumer sells to another through a website, the transaction is customer-to-customer (C2C) commerce.

questions.q: ShopKart, an online store, places orders with manufacturers through its website, sells to customers online, and lets its staff apply for leave through the company intranet.
p: (a) Ordering stock from manufacturers online belongs to which category of e-business?
b2b|b to b|business to business|business-to-business
(b) Selling to customers online belongs to which category?
b2c|b to c|business to customer|business to consumer|business-to-customer
(c) Staff applying for leave on the intranet belongs to which category?
intra-b|intra b|intrab|intra-business|intra business|intra-organisational
questions.e: B2B covers dealings between firms, B2C covers firm-to-customer dealings, and intra-B covers transactions within the firm.

questions.t: Social Responsibility of Business and Business Ethics
questions.q: The obligation of a business to make decisions and act in ways that are desirable in terms of the values and objectives of society is called social ______.
questions.e: Social responsibility goes beyond legal duties and means business acting in the interest of society.

questions.t: Social Responsibility of Business and Business Ethics
questions.q: Paying taxes honestly and on time and respecting the laws of the land is the responsibility of business towards the ______.
questions.e: Business must function as a law-abiding citizen, paying taxes and dues honestly, as part of its responsibility to the government.

questions.t: Social Responsibility of Business and Business Ethics
questions.q: Without any legal requirement, a company in Chennai donates ₹10 lakh to a flood relief fund. Under the classification of social responsibility, this is ______ responsibility.
questions.e: Discretionary responsibility is purely voluntary, such as charity and helping in calamities.

questions.t: Social Responsibility of Business and Business Ethics
questions.q: A company avoids advertisements that hurt religious sentiments, even though no law prohibits them. This reflects ______ responsibility.
questions.e: Ethical responsibility covers behaviour that society expects but which is not required by law, like respecting religious sentiments in advertising.

questions.t: Social Responsibility of Business and Business Ethics
questions.q: Kapoor Textiles of Surat pays a fair dividend to its owners, provides safe working conditions to its staff, and sells good quality cloth at reasonable prices.
p: (a) Paying a fair return on investment is responsibility towards which group?
shareholders|owners|investors|shareholders or owners
(b) Providing safe working conditions is responsibility towards which group?
workers|employees|worker|employee
(c) Selling good quality goods at reasonable prices is responsibility towards which group?
consumers|customers|consumer|customer
questions.e: A business has responsibilities towards different interest groups: owners, workers, consumers, government and the community.

questions.q: Funds required for buying land, buildings and machinery are called ______ capital.
questions.e: Fixed capital requirements are for long-term assets, while working capital is needed for day-to-day operations.

questions.q: An instrument acknowledging a loan taken by a company, carrying a fixed rate of interest, is called a ______.
questions.e: Debentures are borrowed funds; debenture holders are creditors who get fixed interest regardless of profits.

questions.q: Shareholders who have voting rights, are the real owners of the company and get dividend only after preference shareholders hold ______ shares.
questions.e: Equity shareholders bear the highest risk, have voting rights and are paid dividend and capital last.

questions.q: An unsecured promissory note issued by large creditworthy companies to raise short-term funds is called ______.
questions.e: Commercial paper is a short-term unsecured money-market instrument issued at a discount by firms with high credit ratings.

questions.q: A shoe company buys leather worth ₹2,00,000 from a supplier and is allowed to pay after 60 days. Which source of short-term finance is used?
questions.e: Trade credit is credit extended by one trader to another when goods are bought without immediate payment.

questions.q: Shakti Ltd. issues 10,000 debentures of ₹100 each carrying 9% interest per annum.
p: (a) Calculate the annual interest payable (in ₹).
(b) Must this interest be paid even if the company suffers a loss? (yes/no)
yes
(c) Debenture holders are owners or creditors of the company?
creditors|creditor
questions.e: Interest = 10,000 × ₹100 × 9% = ₹90,000; debenture interest is a fixed charge payable even in a loss year because debenture holders are creditors.

questions.q: Which apex bank provides credit for agriculture as well as small, cottage and village industries in rural areas?
questions.a: nabard|national bank for agriculture and rural development
questions.e: NABARD was set up in 1982 to promote integrated rural development, including rural small industries.

questions.q: The bank set up as the principal financial institution for promotion, financing and development of small-scale industries in India is ______.
questions.a: sidbi|small industries development bank of india
questions.e: SIDBI provides direct and indirect financial assistance to the small-scale sector.

questions.q: Micro, small and medium enterprises in India are defined under the ______ Development Act, 2006.
questions.a: msmed|msme|micro small and medium enterprises|micro, small and medium enterprises
questions.e: The MSMED Act, 2006 classifies enterprises as micro, small or medium on the basis of investment (and now turnover).

questions.q: Sunita makes pickles at home in her village using family members as workers, simple tools and local raw materials. Such units are called ______ industries.
questions.e: Cottage (rural or traditional) industries are run by individuals with family labour, little capital and simple equipment, often at home.

questions.q: A trader who buys goods in bulk from manufacturers and sells them in smaller lots to retailers is a ______.
questions.e: Wholesalers link producers and retailers, buying in large quantities and selling in smaller lots.

questions.q: Large retail establishments with a number of departments under one roof, each specialising in a particular line of products, are called ______ stores.
questions.e: Departmental stores offer a wide variety of goods in separate departments under one roof and one management.

questions.q: From which date was the Goods and Services Tax (GST) introduced in India?
questions.e: GST, a destination-based single tax on supply of goods and services, came into force in India on 1 July 2017.

questions.q: Rohit notices that Bata shops in Delhi, Mumbai and Chennai look alike, sell the same products at the same prices and are controlled by a head office. Such shops are called multiple shops or ______ stores.
questions.e: Multiple shops or chain stores are branches of one organisation with uniform appearance, products and prices, centrally managed.

questions.q: Hari sells cheap toys and stationery every day on the pavement outside a school in Lucknow; he has no permanent shop. Among itinerant retailers, he is classified as a ______.
questions.a: street trader|street traders|pavement vendor|pavement vendors|street vendor|street vendors
questions.e: Street traders sit at busy places like footpaths and sell low-priced common-use goods; peddlers move door to door and market traders go to markets on fixed days.

questions.q: Buying goods from a foreign country is called ______.
questions.e: Import trade means purchasing goods from other countries; export means selling goods abroad.

questions.q: A Singapore firm imports crude rubber from Malaysia and, after light processing, exports it to European countries. This is called ______ trade.
questions.e: Entrepot trade means importing goods for the purpose of re-exporting them, often after some processing.

questions.q: An Indian exporter needs a document certifying that the goods were produced in India so that the importing country can grant tariff concessions. This document is the certificate of ______.
questions.e: A certificate of origin specifies the country of production and helps the importer claim tariff concessions.

questions.q: Sharma Exports of Tiruppur receives an order for cotton T-shirts from a buyer in the UK.
p: (a) The importer's bank sends a document guaranteeing payment to the exporter. Name it (letter of ______).
credit|letter of credit|lc
(b) The shipping company issues a document acknowledging receipt of goods on board the ship. Name it.
bill of lading|b/l|bl
(c) For India, is this an import or export transaction?
export|exports
questions.e: A letter of credit assures payment to the exporter; a bill of lading is the shipping company's receipt for goods on board, and selling abroad is export trade.

questions.q: Completing a task on time is effectiveness, while completing it with the minimum use of resources and cost is ______.
questions.e: Effectiveness is about achieving goals on time; efficiency is about doing the task with the least cost and resources.

questions.q: The force that binds all the other functions of management together is called the essence of management, or ______.
questions.e: Coordination synchronises the activities of different departments and runs through all functions of management.

questions.q: The CEO of Surya Ltd. decides to enter the rural market. The production head then prepares departmental plans and instructs supervisors to carry them out. The production head belongs to the ______ level of management.
questions.e: Middle-level managers (departmental heads) interpret top management's policies and assign duties to supervisors.

questions.q: Who is known as the father of general management?
questions.e: Henri Fayol, a French mining engineer, gave 14 general principles of management applicable to all organisations.

questions.q: How many principles of management were given by Henri Fayol?
questions.e: Fayol gave 14 principles, such as division of work, unity of command, unity of direction and scalar chain.

questions.q: Fayol's principle that each group of activities having the same objective must have one head and one plan is unity of ______.
questions.e: Unity of direction means one head and one plan for a group of activities with the same objective; it is different from unity of command.

questions.q: Taylor's wage technique that pays a higher rate per unit to workers who meet or exceed the standard output and a lower rate to those below it is called the ______ system.
questions.a: differential piece wage|differential piece wage system|differential piece rate|differential piece rate system
questions.e: The differential piece wage system distinguishes efficient from inefficient workers and motivates them to reach the standard.

questions.q: Under the differential piece wage system, the standard output is 10 units a day. Workers get ₹50 per unit if they meet the standard and ₹40 per unit if they do not. Arjun makes 11 units and Karan makes 9 units. How many rupees more does Arjun earn than Karan?
A manager at a Pune factory uses a stop-watch to determine the standard time taken by an average worker to complete each part of a job. Which technique of scientific management is this?
questions.e: Time study determines the standard time for a well-defined job, which helps fix a fair day's work and wages.

questions.q: In Sunrise Ltd., Ravi, a production supervisor, receives conflicting orders from both the marketing head and the finance head, and is confused about whom to obey.
p: (a) Which principle of Fayol is being violated?
unity of command
(b) Which technique of Taylor deliberately gives each worker several specialist bosses?
functional foremanship
(c) How many specialists are there under that technique?
questions.e: Fayol's unity of command says one subordinate should have only one boss; Taylor's functional foremanship separates planning and execution with 8 specialist foremen.

questions.q: Growing health awareness in Indian cities has increased the demand for organic food, green tea and fitness equipment. Which dimension of the business environment does this reflect?
questions.e: The social environment includes customs, values and lifestyle trends such as health consciousness, which create new opportunities.

questions.q: Maruti Udyog became the leader in the small car market because it was the first to recognise the need for small cars in India. This shows which importance of understanding the business environment?
questions.a: identifying opportunities and getting the first mover advantage
o: assisting in planning and policy formulation
questions.e: Understanding the environment enables a firm to identify opportunities early and gain the first mover advantage, as Maruti did.

questions.q: Under the New Economic Policy of 1991, the government of India abolished industrial licensing for most industries, sold part of its shareholding in public sector units, and reduced import duties.
p: (a) Abolishing industrial licensing is part of which policy?
liberalisation|liberalization
(b) Selling part of the government's shares in public sector units is part of which policy?
privatisation|privatization|disinvestment
(c) Reducing import duties to integrate with the world economy is part of which policy?
globalisation|globalization
questions.e: The 1991 reforms were built on liberalisation (freeing from controls), privatisation (greater role of private sector) and globalisation (integration with the world economy).

questions.q: A plan that states expected results in numerical terms, such as expected sales of ₹50 lakh in a year, is a ______.
questions.e: A budget is a statement of expected results expressed in numbers; it is both a plan and a control device.

questions.q: A specific statement that tells what must or must not be done, leaving no scope for discretion, such as 'No smoking inside the factory', is a ______.
questions.e: Rules are rigid and must be followed; violation usually leads to a penalty.

questions.q: A company decides that it will recruit only graduates for its junior management positions. This general guideline that sets the boundaries for decision-making is a ______.
questions.e: Policies are general statements that guide thinking and decision-making, such as a recruitment policy.

questions.q: ABC Ltd. wants to increase its sales by 10% this year. To face a rival's new product, it decides on a comprehensive plan of TV advertising and price cuts, keeping in mind that planning always deals with the future.
p: (a) The aim of increasing sales by 10% is which type of plan?
objective|objectives
(b) The comprehensive plan to deal with the rival's new product is which type of plan?
strategy|strategies
(c) Planning deals with the future. Which feature of planning is this? (planning is ______)
futuristic|future oriented|forward looking|future-oriented
questions.e: Objectives are end results; a strategy is a comprehensive plan to achieve objectives in view of the environment; planning is futuristic as it looks ahead.

questions.q: The grouping of similar activities into jobs and jobs into departments is called ______.
questions.e: Departmentalisation groups similar or related jobs into units like production, finance and marketing.

questions.q: In the delegation of authority, which element can never be delegated?
questions.e: Authority can be delegated, but accountability cannot; the superior remains answerable for the work delegated.

questions.q: The systematic delegation of authority to the lowest levels throughout the organisation is called ______.
questions.e: Decentralisation is the extension of delegation to all levels, giving lower levels decision-making power.

questions.q: A company makes cosmetics, garments and footwear, and sets up a separate unit with its own production, finance and marketing for each product. Which organisational structure is it using?
questions.e: A divisional structure groups activities by product lines, each division being responsible for its own profit or loss.

questions.q: The process of searching for prospective employees and stimulating them to apply for jobs is called ______.
questions.e: Recruitment builds a pool of applicants; selection then chooses the most suitable from them.

questions.q: Training in which employees learn on equipment similar to that used on the job, but in a separate area away from the actual workplace, is ______ training.
questions.e: Vestibule training is an off-the-job method used for costly or delicate equipment so that production is not disturbed.

questions.q: Recruitment is called a positive process, while selection is called a ______ process because it rejects many applicants.
questions.e: Selection eliminates unsuitable candidates at each stage, so it is considered a negative process.

questions.q: A bank fills a vacancy in its Jaipur branch by shifting an officer from its Kota branch at the same level and pay. Which internal source of recruitment is used?
questions.e: Transfer is the shifting of an employee from one job or place to another without change in responsibility or pay.

questions.q: How many levels of needs are there in Maslow's need hierarchy theory?
questions.e: Maslow's five needs are physiological, safety, belongingness, esteem and self-actualisation.

questions.q: According to Maslow, the need for affection, acceptance and friendship is the ______ need.
questions.e: Belongingness (social) needs come after safety needs and relate to affection, acceptance and friendship.

questions.q: The leadership style in which the leader gives orders and expects subordinates to obey them without question is ______ leadership.
questions.e: An autocratic leader centralises decision-making and uses one-way communication.

questions.q: Infosys offers its employees company shares at a price lower than the market price. Which financial incentive is this?
questions.a: co-partnership|co partnership|stock option|stock options|employee stock option|esop
questions.e: Co-partnership or stock options let employees own a part of the company, creating a sense of ownership.

questions.q: In Sharma Enterprises, a worker's complaint travels through the supervisor and manager to the director. Meanwhile, rumours of a bonus spread quickly through casual chats among workers. Some instructions are misunderstood because the words used have different meanings.
p: (a) Communication that follows the chain of command is which type?
formal|formal communication
(b) What is the informal communication network called?
grapevine
(c) Misunderstanding due to words with different meanings is which type of barrier?
semantic|semantic barrier|semantic barriers
questions.e: Formal communication flows through official channels; informal communication is called the grapevine; semantic barriers arise from problems in encoding and decoding messages.

questions.q: Controlling is both a forward looking and a ______ looking function.
questions.e: Controlling compares past performance with standards and also improves future performance.

questions.q: Planning and controlling are inseparable: planning without controlling is meaningless, and controlling without ______ is blind.
questions.e: Plans provide the standards for control, and control checks whether plans are being followed.

questions.q: In a Ludhiana factory, the standard output is 200 units per day but actual output is 180 units. The manager ignores a 1% rise in stationery expenses but takes action on the output shortfall.
p: (a) Calculate the percentage deviation in output.
(b) Attending only to significant deviations is called management by ______.
exception
(c) Focusing control on key result areas like output is called ______ control.
critical point|critical-point
questions.e: Deviation = (200 − 180)/200 × 100 = 10%; management by exception focuses on significant deviations, and critical point control focuses on key result areas.

questions.q: The decision regarding how much of the profit is to be distributed to shareholders and how much is to be retained is the ______ decision.
questions.e: The dividend decision divides earnings between dividends to shareholders and retained earnings.

questions.q: Long-term investment decisions, such as buying a new machine or opening a new plant, are also called ______ decisions.
questions.e: Capital budgeting decisions involve huge amounts, affect long-term growth and are irreversible except at a high cost.

questions.q: A company has EBIT of ₹5,00,000, 10% debentures of ₹10,00,000 and a tax rate of 30%. Calculate its profit after tax in ₹.

Vardhan Ltd. needs ₹50 lakh. Its expected return on investment is 15%, the tax rate is 30% and equity shares are of ₹10 each. Plan I: all equity (5,00,000 shares). Plan II: ₹25 lakh equity (2,50,000 shares) and ₹25 lakh 10% debt.
p: (a) Calculate EBIT in ₹.
(b) Calculate EPS under Plan I in ₹.
(c) Calculate EPS under Plan II in ₹.
questions.e: EBIT = 15% of ₹50 lakh = ₹7,50,000. Plan I: EAT = ₹5,25,000, EPS = ₹1.05. Plan II: interest ₹2,50,000, EBT ₹5,00,000, EAT ₹3,50,000, EPS = ₹1.40. EPS rises because ROI exceeds the cost of debt (trading on equity).

questions.q: The market in which securities are issued for the first time is the ______ market.
questions.e: The primary or new issue market deals with fresh securities; the secondary market deals with already-issued securities.

questions.q: The statutory body that regulates the securities market in India is ______.
questions.a: sebi|securities and exchange board of india
questions.e: SEBI, given statutory powers in 1992, protects investors and regulates and develops the securities market.

questions.q: The money market instrument issued by the RBI on behalf of the Government of India to meet short-term borrowing needs, with maturities like 91, 182 and 364 days, is the ______.
questions.e: Treasury bills are zero-coupon instruments issued at a discount and redeemed at par.

questions.q: Tata Steel offers new shares to its existing shareholders in proportion to the shares they already hold. This method of floatation is a ______.
questions.e: In a rights issue, existing shareholders get the privilege to buy new shares in proportion to their holdings.

questions.q: The four Ps of the marketing mix are product, price, place and ______.
questions.e: The marketing mix consists of product, price, place (physical distribution) and promotion.

questions.q: The marketing philosophy which holds that a firm should identify and satisfy customer needs better than its competitors is the ______ concept.
questions.e: The marketing concept starts with the customer's needs and aims at profit through customer satisfaction.

questions.q: A brand or part of a brand that is given legal protection so that no one else can use it is a ______.
questions.e: A registered trademark gives the firm exclusive legal right to use the brand name or mark.

questions.q: A shoe company sells its products to customers only through its own retail outlets, without any middlemen. Which channel of distribution is this?
questions.e: A zero-level or direct channel involves no intermediaries between manufacturer and consumer.

questions.q: Maya Foods launches a new mango juice. It distributes free sample sachets in markets, offers 'buy two, get one free', and gets favourable news stories about the juice published in newspapers. The juice comes in an attractive tetra pack that protects and promotes it.
p: (a) Free samples and 'buy two, get one free' are tools of which element of the promotion mix?
sales promotion
(b) Getting favourable news stories published is part of which element of the promotion mix?
public relations|publicity|pr
(c) Designing the container of the product is called ______.
packaging
questions.e: Sales promotion gives short-term incentives; public relations builds goodwill through publicity; packaging protects the product and helps promote it.

questions.q: In which year was the Consumer Protection Act currently in force in India passed?
questions.e: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced the Act of 1986.

questions.q: The quality certification mark of the Bureau of Indian Standards for industrial and consumer products like electrical appliances is the ______ mark.
questions.e: The ISI mark shows that a product conforms to the standards set by the Bureau of Indian Standards.

questions.q: The quality certification mark used for agricultural products like spices, honey and pulses is ______.
questions.e: Agmark certifies the quality of agricultural produce; FPO is for processed fruit products and Hallmark for gold jewellery.

questions.q: Kavita bought a mixer-grinder for ₹4,000 from a shop in Bhopal. It stopped working within a week, and the shopkeeper refused to replace it.
p: (a) Which consumer right does Kavita exercise by filing a complaint?
right to seek redressal|seek redressal|redressal|right to redressal
(b) Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, which commission should she approach?
district commission|district|district consumer disputes redressal commission
(c) An appeal against an order of the National Commission lies with which court?
supreme court|supreme court of india
questions.e: The right to seek redressal lets consumers get relief for defective goods; a claim of this size goes to the District Commission, and appeals against National Commission orders lie with the Supreme Court.
